scenes.heading: End-to-End DataOps Deployment
scenes.narration: This is where everything converges: containers, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD, and GitOps combine into one coherent DataOps deployment.

scenes.heading: The full stack
bullets: Kubernetes runs and schedules the workloads
CI/CD and GitOps deliver changes continuously
scenes.narration: Terraform provisions the cloud foundation, from networking to the warehouse and the Kubernetes cluster itself. Docker packages every pipeline component into reproducible images. Kubernetes runs and schedules those workloads, including jobs and cronjobs for batch data. And CI/CD together with GitOps deliver changes continuously and safely on top of it all.

scenes.heading: Commit to production, end to end
scenes.narration: An engineer commits both application code and SQL models. CI runs the full test suite and builds a versioned image on success. That image is pushed and the GitOps repository is updated with the new tag. Argo CD detects the change and syncs the cluster to match. Finally observability watches the release and triggers an automatic rollback if health degrades.

scenes.heading: The GitOps deploy manifest
scenes.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: pipeline-runner
  namespace: data
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: runner
          image: registry.example.com/acme/pipeline:2.3.1
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: warehouse-creds
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
scenes.narration: This manifest, committed to the GitOps repo, ties the concepts together. It pins an exact image version so deployments are reproducible. It pulls credentials from a Kubernetes secret rather than embedding them. And it defines a readiness probe so traffic only flows once the pod is truly ready. Changing that image tag in Git is all it takes to trigger a controlled production rollout.

scenes.heading: Siloed tools vs unified DataOps
scenes.narration: When tools are siloed, teams rely on manual handoffs, environments drift apart, and releases stay slow and risky. A unified DataOps approach automates the flow end to end, treats Git as the single source of truth, and makes every release fast, safe, and fully auditable.

scenes.text: Great DataOps is one automated path from commit to production, with Git as the source of truth and observability closing the loop.
scenes.narration: Great DataOps boils down to one automated path from commit to production, with Git as the source of truth and observability closing the loop back to the developer.
